ABOUT

Understanding systems by building them

I'm Rohan Sapkal, a Computer Engineering student focused on cybersecurity, network security, and security research.

I enjoy going beyond theory and understanding how systems actually behave — how networks communicate, how services expose themselves, how attacks work, and how defensive controls can detect and respond to them.

My work spans Linux-based security labs, network traffic analysis, DNS security, security automation, and behavioral threat detection. I've built hands-on projects involving SSH monitoring, DNS spoofing simulation, network analysis, and Linux security, while also exploring cybersecurity through research.

I'm particularly interested in the intersection of network security, system defense, and intelligent threat detection, and I'm continuously building labs and projects to turn concepts into practical experience.

I've also contributed to research on stealthy insider threats and UEBA-based detection in enterprise environments.

RESEARCH

UEBA-based insider threat detection

expand ⤢

Presented at the 11th International Conference on ICT for Intelligent Systems (ICTIS), 9–11 April 2026, Bangkok, Thailand — selected for publication via Springer.

ROLE · CORE RESEARCH CONTRIBUTOR

An Adversarial Evaluation of Stealthy Insider Attacks and UEBA-Based Defensive Detection in Enterprise Environments

This research examines how stealthy insider activity — misuse of legitimate credentials, privilege misuse, persistence, covert communication, and temporal evasion — can remain difficult to detect at the individual event level, and how User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) can improve detection by looking at cumulative behavioral deviation instead of isolated events.

The work builds behavioral baselines, analyzes deviation from those baselines, and applies cumulative risk scoring, evaluated through a Red Team / Blue Team methodology with longitudinal behavioral correlation across simulated enterprise activity.

Stealthy insider threatsLegitimate credential misusePrivilege misuse PersistenceCovert communicationTemporal evasion Behavioral baselinesDeviation analysisCumulative risk scoring Red Team / Blue TeamLongitudinal correlation

Presented as research analysis, not a claim of universal detection effectiveness. No experimental metrics beyond what is documented in the paper are represented here.

Co-authored with: Asmit Patil, Smita Shedbale, Sneha Kumbhar, Ashwini Athawale, Smita Arude, Rohan S. Sapkal, Priya Sharma, and Dhanaraj Jadhav. Author order reflects the published listing only, not ranked contribution.
